chunk_findings.detail: The added queue design makes each queued waiter hold an flock on its ticket file while waiting and poll every `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` seconds. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which states agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. With multiple CI runs queued for the full-suite lock, every queued agent polls at 4 Hz while holding a lock, which is exactly the pattern the guidance forbids.

chunk_findings.detail: The new code constructs `SuiteBusy(_holders(directory, limit), time.monotonic() - start, position)` both in the `say(...)` call and in the `raise`. The previous implementation called `SuiteBusy(holders, elapsed)` with only two arguments, and this diff does not update the `SuiteBusy` class. With any non-first waiter, the first time `position != said` it tries to build the exception and gets a `TypeError` instead of a `SuiteBusy` refusal, so the queue wait can crash before timing out or notifying.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: In `_live`, a `.ticket` is unlinked whenever `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` can acquire the lock; `age` is checked only on `LockTimeout`. A new or reclaimed `.ticket` is briefly an unlocked file between the rename/open in `_Ticket.__init__`/`__enter__` and the owner actually acquiring the flock. If another waiter scans in that window, it locks and deletes the ticket. The just-created waiter then has no visible directory entry, `_beat` fails on the missing path, and later `_live` scans never include it, so it is treated as last and can be passed by later arrivals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: When a waiter times out, `_Ticket.__exit__` renames `self.path` to `.parked` without first calling `_beat`. The parked file keeps the last heartbeat `st_mtime`, not the parking time. If the final `_live()` scan before timeout takes longer than `grace_s`, the just-created parked file is already older than `grace_s`, so the next scanner treats it as expired and deletes it, losing the kept queue place.

chunk_findings.detail: The wait `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 1)` is not a valid barrier here. The first `early` attempt at line 138 has already created a `.ticket` file; for the later retry to keep its place, that ticket must still exist as `*.ticket` after `SuiteBusy`. Therefore `_tickets(tmp_path)` is already `1` before `late = _waiter(...)` is started, so this wait can return immediately before `late` has actually enqueued. The following `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 2)` can then be satisfied by the retained `early` ticket plus `late`'s new ticket before the `early` retry thread is scheduled; the outer holder is released with only `late` ready, making `order == ["early", "late"]` flaky or failing. The condition after starting `late` should require a count that cannot be satisfied by the retained early ticket (or otherwise wait for `late` to have its own ticket), otherwise the test does not exercise the intended “retry keeps place” interleaving deterministically.

chunk_findings.detail: The new FIFO wait path violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] (“agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting”): `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` introduces a 250 ms polling loop, and the module docstring says each waiter “holds an flock on it” while queued. For example, with `max_concurrent_suites=1`, a second suite waits by polling/touching every 250 ms while retaining its ticket flock; a stopped waiter can then hold a live flock without heartbeating, forcing reliance on the added stale-timeout heuristic instead of an event-driven wakeup.

chunk_findings.detail: A newly created but not yet flocked ticket is omitted from `live` while age <= `NEW_S`; only an unlocked ticket older than `NEW_S` is unlinked. This lets a later process overtake an earlier one. Interleaving: waiter A enters `_Ticket.__enter__`, where `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` has created `000...-a.ticket` but A is descheduled between file creation and taking the flock; waiter B then enters with a later timestamp, scans, sees A’s unlocked young ticket and neither appends nor removes it, so `line` is `[B]`, `position == 1`, and B acquires a free slot before A. The arrival order is broken.

chunk_findings.detail: The `.parked` branch unlinks any parked file older than `grace_s` without first checking whether it is currently locked for reuse. `_Ticket.__enter__` locks `self._parked` before renaming it to `.ticket`, so a scanner can unlink the parked file after that lock is acquired but before the rename. The retry then suppresses the rename `OSError` and the missing-path `_beat`, and enters `hold` with no visible ticket; `position = len(line) + 1` can make it lose the kept place. This is triggered by a retry racing with a scan after its parked ticket exceeds `grace_s`.

chunk_findings.detail: `_Ticket.__enter__` uses `self._lock.enter_context(fsio.file_lock(self._parked or self.path, 0))` with a nonblocking lock and no retry, while `_live` deliberately takes `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` on unlocked `.ticket` files (and can race with reclaiming `.parked` files). This is the unaddressed version of the parked-file race: the current code only protects after the claim is already locked, not between `_parked_for` returning the path and `__enter__` acquiring the lock.

chunk_findings.detail: A legitimate new waiter can be aborted by the scanner. For a new ticket, `_Ticket.__init__` does not create `self.path`; `fsio.file_lock(self.path, 0)` must create and lock the file. The path is visible after creation but before the lock is held. Another waiter's `_live` can see that just-created `.ticket`, and its “created, its owner has not locked it yet” branch calls `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` itself. If that scanner wins the flock first, the new owner's own `fsio.file_lock` then raises `fsio.LockTimeout`, which `_Ticket.__enter__` does not catch or retry. The new waiter then fails before entering the queue even though it did nothing wrong.

chunk_findings.detail: The watcher captures the owner PID with `owner = os.getppid()` when the script first runs. If the owner is SIGKILLed after `subprocess.Popen` for the watcher returns but before that first statement executes, the watcher has already been reparented, so `os.getppid()` returns PID 1 (or a subreaper). The watcher then never sees a parent change and never calls `os.killpg`, leaving the orphaned command group alive—the exact failure this code was added to fix. chunk_findings.detail: The watcher `Popen` handle is discarded and never waited for. The watcher starts by sleeping 1 second before its first group check, so it is still running when the temporary `Popen` object is deallocated; Python does not reap it later. chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify the whole process group is killed, but it never records the PID of the actual `sleep 600` process. chunk_findings.detail: The shell command embeds `pids` unquoted: `f"sleep 600 & echo $! >> {pids}; echo $$ >> {pids}; wait"`.
